name: Viking 1
tagline: First successful Mars lander; biology experiments
dispatch: Viking 1 solved the problem nothing had solved: how to land on Mars and live. The Soviet landers before it had died within about twenty seconds of touchdown, returning only a featureless grey frame; Viking had to descend through an atmosphere too thin to rely on and too thick to ignore, and it did it with a first-of-its-kind sequence — an aeroshell to survive entry, a parachute for the middle of the fall, and throttled rocket engines to set its three legs down softly at the end. It was two machines in one, an orbiter to survey and relay and a lander to work the ground, and it carried the first laboratory ever sent to test another planet’s soil for life. Every Mars landing since has flown some version of the descent Viking proved.
description: The first successful Mars lander mission, on the surface from July 1976 through November 1982. Carried four biology experiments and returned high-resolution images of the Chryse Planitia plains. The Viking 1 / Viking 2 pair set the template for every Mars lander that followed.
best_known_for: First successful Mars lander; biology experiments
